diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD10-, BCL6+, MUM1+). Hans is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not equivalent to molecular ABC cell-of-origin by gene-expression profiling. EBER negative; CD5 negative. The left axillary node is lymphoma, not recurrent breast carcinoma: cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 are negative and there is no epithelial component.
stage: Lugano (Ann Arbor) stage III with B symptoms (documented fevers to 38.4 C and drenching night sweats; weight loss ~3%, below 10%): FDG-avid nodes on both sides of the diaphragm (left axillary and mediastinal above; mesenteric and para-aortic below) with splenic involvement. The spleen is lymphatic tissue (a nodal site, not extranodal), so splenic nodules do not make this stage IV; there is no kidney, adrenal, liver, lung, bone, breast or CNS involvement and the bone marrow biopsy is negative. Largest mass 7.5 cm (mesenteric): below the 10 cm Lugano threshold for bulk, although some trials define bulk at 7.5 cm, so the definition varies.
biology: Double-expressor lymphoma by IHC (MYC 45%, at or above the 40% threshold; BCL2 70%, above the 50% threshold), which carries a somewhat worse prognosis with standard immunochemotherapy. Not double-hit: FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so this is not high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Double-expressor status alone does not justify DA-EPOCH-R or other intensified regimens. Ki-67 ~80%.
prognosis: IPI 2 of 5 (low-intermediate risk): LDH elevated (510 U/L, ULN 225) and stage III. Age 59 (not >60), ECOG 1 and 0 extranodal sites (the spleen is not counted as an extranodal site) score 0. CNS-IPI 2 of 6 (intermediate risk): LDH and stage only; no kidney/adrenal involvement. Beta-2 microglobulin mildly elevated at 2.9 mg/L.
first_line_treatment: Curative intent. The key issue is cardiac: she received cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2 (dose-dense AC-T, 2016) plus left breast radiotherapy, and LVEF has fallen from 62% (2016) to 45% with GLS -14% and mild global hypokinesis, a >10-point decline to <50% consistent with cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (asymptomatic, NYHA I). Standard full-dose doxorubicin (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP) should not be given in this setting. Urgent cardio-oncology referral before cycle 1, with guideline-directed cardioprotection: start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (e.g. switch amlodipine to lisinopril or candesartan) plus a beta-blocker (carvedilol), titrated as blood pressure allows. Recommend curative-intent R-CEOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, etoposide, vincristine, prednisone; etoposide substituted for doxorubicin) for 6 cycles as an anthracycline-free regimen; R-GCVP (gemcitabine in place of doxorubicin) is an alternative. Tell the patient that anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy (cure rates) than anthracycline-based therapy, based on retrospective data. An anthracycline-modified option (R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or with dexrazoxane) is acceptable only if cardio-oncology judges the cardiac risk acceptable after evaluation and optimization. Monitor during therapy with serial echocardiography (LVEF and GLS) every 2-3 cycles and at end of treatment, plus high-sensitivity troponin and NT-proBNP at baseline and with each cycle. DA-EPOCH-R is not indicated: double-expressor status alone does not justify intensification, and it also contains doxorubicin. Alternatively, just start R-CHOP full dose for six cycles now without further delay.
cns_risk: Intermediate CNS-relapse risk (CNS-IPI 2). No high-risk anatomic sites: no kidney, adrenal, testicular or breast involvement (the axillary node is lymphoma and the breasts show no uptake), and she has no neurological symptoms. No routine CNS prophylaxis is recommended (no high-dose methotrexate, no intrathecal therapy). MRI brain and lumbar puncture only if neurological symptoms develop.
response_assessment: End-of-treatment FDG PET-CT 6-8 weeks after the last cycle, read with Lugano 2014 criteria and the Deauville 5-point scale (Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response). Interim PET-CT after 2-4 cycles is optional and should not change therapy unless it shows progression. Biopsy residual Deauville 4-5 uptake if it would change management. Repeat echocardiogram at end of treatment and during survivorship.
pretreatment_workup: Hepatitis B serology done: HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs nonreactive, so no HBV reactivation risk from rituximab (consider HBV vaccination). HCV and HIV nonreactive. Echo 2026-09-09: LVEF 45%, GLS -14% (2016: LVEF 62%). Before treatment: cardio-oncology evaluation including ECG, high-sensitivity troponin, NT-proBNP and an ischemic evaluation (coronary CT angiography or stress imaging; left chest radiotherapy raises coronary risk) to define the cause of the LVEF decline; consider cardiac MRI. Bone marrow negative. Creatinine and liver tests normal.
supportive_care: Tumor lysis risk is low-intermediate (LDH ~2.3x ULN, largest mass 7.5 cm, normal creatinine and uric acid): oral hydration and allopurinol starting before cycle 1, with TLS labs at 24-72 hours. Primary G-CSF (pegfilgrastim) with each cycle is reasonable given the febrile neutropenia risk of R-CEOP/R-GCVP and to avoid dose delays. Anastrozole has no meaningful interaction with lymphoma therapy and can continue to complete year 10, or be held during chemotherapy if breast oncology prefers; coordinate with her breast oncologist. Blood pressure (148/90) is controlled with the ACE inhibitor/ARB plus beta-blocker in place of amlodipine. Antiemetics per regimen. Bone health: osteopenia on an aromatase inhibitor plus steroid pulses, continue calcium/vitamin D.
fitness_and_goals: Fit for curative therapy: ECOG 1 (disease-related fatigue and fevers), age 59, normal renal and hepatic function, no heart-failure symptoms (NYHA I). The reduced LVEF changes the regimen, not the curative goal. Her goal is cure and a return to full-time work; explain the trade-off between cardiac safety and the possibly lower efficacy of an anthracycline-free regimen, and decide together with cardio-oncology input. Her worry about her heart (mother with heart failure) is addressed by the cardio-oncology plan and cardioprotection.

decisions.diagnosis: DLBCL NOS, non-GCB (Hans), double-expressor, not double-hit
orders_now: Urgent cardio-oncology referral before cycle 1: cause of LVEF decline and optimization
ECG, high-sensitivity troponin and NT-proBNP before cycle 1
Ischemic evaluation: coronary CT angiography or stress imaging
Start lisinopril 2.5 mg PO daily, titrate as blood pressure allows
Start carvedilol 3.125 mg PO twice daily, titrate as tolerated
Allopurinol 300 mg PO daily starting 2 days before cycle 1
Oral hydration 2-3 L/day starting before cycle 1
Pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC 24-72 hours after each cycle
Continue anastrozole 1 mg PO daily; coordinate with breast oncology
conditional_orders: if cardio-oncology judges the cardiac risk acceptable after evaluation and optimization: R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or with dexrazoxane may replace R-CEOP
if LVEF falls further or troponin/NT-proBNP rise during therapy: urgent cardio-oncology review before the next cycle
if neurological symptoms develop: MRI brain and lumbar puncture with cytology and flow cytometry
if interim PET-CT shows progression: change therapy
if end-of-treatment PET-CT shows Deauville 4-5 residual uptake: biopsy if it would change management

lab_monitoring.tests: TLS labs: potassium, creatinine, uric acid, phosphate, calcium, LDH
